items.claim: The single-verse span is sound, and the root echo with 27:2 is correctly framed as texture rather than adopted cohesion.
items.evidence: 27:1's hitpael תתהלל ("boast") and 27:2's piel יהללך ("let him praise you") share the root הלל but the doubled-tav hitpael pattern versus the bare piel prefix mark a real binyan difference, so the rejected cluster candidate is a genuine rival, correctly declined. The preceding verse 26:28 shares no skeleton token with 27:1, so the front boundary is undisputed and both seams are accounted for.

items.claim: The verse is correctly isolated as a single proverb with no skeleton token shared with either neighbor.
items.evidence: Word-by-word skeleton comparison of 27:6 against 27:7, and of 27:8 against 27:7, turns up no shared content token in either direction, matching the row's own claim; the antithetic bicolon (a full soul against a hungry soul) is complete within the verse and both seams are clean.

items.claim: The verse is correctly isolated; neither 27:13 nor 27:15 shares a skeleton token with 27:14.
items.evidence: Skeleton comparison confirms no overlap between 27:14 and either neighbor, so the ironic-reversal saying (a loud-voiced blessing reckoned as a curse) stands complete in-verse with both seams disclosed as clean, consistent with the row's claim.

items.claim: The generic-term rejection of the shared adam token is well-reasoned, but the parenthetical English gloss is set in curly quotes with no web: ref in the same field.
items.evidence: The row's own quoting convention (curly quotes reserved for verbatim WEB text carrying an inline web: ref) is not honored for the parenthetical "the man" gloss attached to האדם (oshb:Prov.27.19) and האדם (oshb:Prov.27.20) -- that gloss needed straight quotes, or a curly quote paired with web:Prov.27.19. The underlying granularity call is otherwise sound: the analogical comparanda check out -- הגו recurs verse-initial at 25:4 and הגו at 25:5, זהב anchors 25:11 and זהב anchors 25:12, and עצל/ועצל/עצל/עצל chain across all four of 26:13-16 -- so the shared man-token's recurrence at 27:19/27:20 is comparatively generic vocabulary and the single_proverb call stands.

items.claim: The verse is correctly isolated and the ketiv/qere note is properly disclosed as non-boundary corroboration.
items.evidence: The inventory lists exactly one ketiv/qere note at 27:20, matching the inline unpointed-then-pointed Abaddon-form pair in the source bytes; skeleton comparison shows no token shared with either 27:19 or 27:21, so the synonymous merism (Sheol and Abaddon, a man's eyes) stands complete in-verse and the K/Q disclosure is correctly framed as not affecting the boundary.

items.claim: The single-verse boundary is sound and the petuchah is correctly disclosed as tier-3 corroboration rather than a driver.
items.evidence: The inventory confirms a lone PE at 27:22, single-witness; skeleton comparison shows 27:22 and 27:23 share no token, corroborating the addressee shift the row itself names -- the third-person fool-saying at 27:22 gives way to the fresh 2ms flock-instruction opening at 27:23.

items.claim: The internal instruction-chain argument for 27:23-27 is byte-accurate, but the row never establishes its own back seam at 28:1, and two English glosses are curly-quoted without the mandatory inline web: ref.
items.evidence: boundary_evidence_refs names only 27:22-27:27; 28:1 is never cited or argued, so the seam warrant is one-sided. Re-derivation does support the break -- 28:1's skeleton shares no token with 27:27's, and 28:1's third-person wicked/righteous sentence drops the 2ms addressee that frames 27:23-27:27 throughout -- but this is exactly the kind of cross-seam disclosure the row owes and does not make. Separately, the rationale's curly-quoted "know well the state of your flocks, set your heart on the herds" is not verbatim web:Prov.27.23, which actually reads “and pay attention to your herds” (web:Prov.27.23) for the second clause, and carries no web: ref anywhere in the field, and the curly-quoted "for riches are not forever" likewise lacks the required inline web: ref even though it does match web:Prov.27.24 -- both spans violate the WEB-quote-verbatim-plus-ref rule, one of them while also blending unmarked paraphrase into what reads as a direct quotation.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary is sound, but the torah-thread's positional claim is arithmetically wrong: the nearest other occurrence is two verses later, not three.
items.evidence: תורה/תורה anchors 28:4 (occurring twice in that verse), תורה anchors 28:7, and תורה anchors 28:9 -- direct inspection of 28:10-28:13 turns up no further torah token in the chapter. From 28:7, the nearest other occurrence is 28:9, two verses later, not three; a three-verse gap instead separates 28:4 from 28:7. The underlying boundary claim is unaffected -- 28:6 and 28:8 share no skeleton token with 28:7 either, so single_proverb still stands -- but the digit in the rationale needs correcting to match the bytes.
